title: Validate metering for compressed and multipart streaming payloads
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Customers may send request payloads that are compressed (gzip) and/or split into multipart streaming frames. There are intermittent billing mismatches and quota anomalies observed when compressed fragments are delivered out-of-order, duplicated, or truncated. This ticket scopes the validation, fixes, and tests required to ensure token and byte accounting is correct for compressed + multipart streams.
background: We currently normalize token counts at the tokenizer stage which assumes an uncompressed canonical byte stream. In streaming with compressed frames the runtime performs incremental decompression and emits logical chunks into the inference pipeline. Edge cases discovered in recent incidents: (1) duplicated compressed frames during network retries get double-counted, (2) truncated last gzip block causes tokenizer to see partial tokens with inconsistent counts, (3) chunk reordering during HTTP/2 multiplexing yields non-monotonic sequence offsets that confuse the metering aggregator. Existing reconciliation jobs correct many cases but not quickly enough for quota enforcement and near-real-time billing dashboards.
proposed_solution: 1) Add deterministic per-fragment metadata at decompression boundary: decompressed_length, crc32_of_fragment, sequence_nonce, and canonical_token_count_hint computed by running the tokenizer on the decompressed fragment. 2) Persist fragment metadata to the streaming-metadata store with idempotency key = (session_id, sequence_nonce, crc32). 3) Update metering aggregator to use persisted fragment metadata for final accounting instead of recomputing from raw frames. 4) Ensure aggregator ignores duplicate fragments (same idempotency key) and supports out-of-order ingestion by summing by canonical sequence number. 5) Add a reconciliation window that detects truncated final block: if final fragment crc mismatch or missing EOF marker after N seconds, mark session as "post-process-required" and run a deterministic healing pass that requests the final fragment from gateway logs or marks session for manual review. 6) Expose a debug flag to include per-fragment accounting in trace events (debug builds only).
tradeoffs:
- Adding per-fragment token hints increases metadata writes (approx +10% write volume for high-churn sessions). We accept additional write cost to avoid expensive re-tokenization and long-running reconciliation.
- Reliance on crc32 and sequence_nonce reduces false dedupes but is not cryptographically strong; for extremely adversarial inputs, additional HMAC could be added later.
- The post-process healing pass adds latency to final billing visibility for a tiny percentage of sessions; we will surface this in the console and billing logs instead of delaying all sessions.
acceptance_criteria: For synthetic compressed+multipart sessions (see test harness) token counts match a canonical offline tokenizer run within 0 token delta for 99.99% of sessions.
Duplicate compressed fragments are not double-counted in final invoices or quota usage (verified with duplicate-injection tests).
Out-of-order fragments are reconciled and produce identical totals to ordered ingestion.
No negative credits or quota reversals occur after normal session completion.
Metering aggregation latency for normal sessions remains within existing SLO (95th percentile +5% acceptable).
test_plan: Unit tests for decompressor boundary that verify crc32 and decompressed_length compute correctly for concatenated gzip members.
Integration tests that run the full pipeline with the synthetic client producing: ordered fragments, reordered fragments, duplicate fragments, truncated last fragment, and interleaved gzip members.
Chaos test: simulate gateway retry duplication and verify aggregator idempotency under 500 sessions/min at peak load.
End-to-end billing smoke: create test account, run a known workload through compressed streaming, verify billing event and dashboard match canonical counts.
Backward compatibility test: sessions without compression must be unaffected (compare metrics before/after rollout).
rollout_plan: Feature-flag the new metadata writes and aggregator path. Deploy decompression metadata writer to staging and run 24h of synthetic load. Enable aggregator path on canary (5% traffic) for 48h while monitoring token-count variance and metering latency. If stable, promote to 25% for 24h, then 100% across regions. Keep reconciliation job enabled during entire rollout and monitor 'post-process-required' rate; aim for <0.01% of sessions. Provide rollback by toggling aggregator path and allowing consumers to fall back to re-tokenization path for 30 minutes while we investigate.
metrics: canonical_token_delta_95pct: difference between pipeline and offline tokenizer at 95th percentile
duplicate_fragment_rate: percent of fragments with repeated idempotency key
post_process_rate: percent of sessions flagged for post-process healing
metering_latency_p95: time from session end to meter finalization
billing_correction_incidents: count of manual invoice adjustments attributed to compressed-streaming bugs
comments: 2025-02-12 Aisha Patel: Triage notes — observed billing mismatch for customer 'AcmeRetail' where duplicated compressed fragments inflated token counts. Root cause unknown; creating ticket to standardize fragment-level accounting.
2025-02-18 Marcus Nguyen: Design review — added crc32 + sequence_nonce proposal. Asked infra for storage estimate; estimated metadata writes +10% on high-churn sessions.
2025-02-21 Infra SIG: Storage impact accepted; suggested batching metadata writes for micro-sessions to reduce load. Marcus to prototype batching in writer.
2025-02-26 QA: Early integration tests show failure mode when client sends concatenated gzip members across frames; tokenizer hint must run per-member not per-frame. Patch submitted in PR #342.

2025-03-02 Marcus Nguyen: Canary started (5%). Initial metrics look good: canonical_token_delta_95pct = 0, duplicate_fragment_rate filtered to zero on canary traffic. No regressions observed. Continuing rollout.
2025-03-02 Sarah Lee (Billing): Please ensure billing exports include flags for 'post_process_required' so downstream finance systems can handle finalization delays. Added to attachments.
